proposals.before: [1] In the third month, on the new moon day yisi, famine in the Southern Metropolitan Region was relieved.
proposals.after: [1] In the third month, on the new moon day jisi, famine in the Southern Metropolitan Region was relieved.
proposals.reason: Chinese calendrical day is 己巳 (jisi); literal wrongly reads 已巳 as yisi.

proposals.before: On jiyou the eunuch Zhang Shan took charge of military affairs; Marquis of Dingxi Jiang Wan became supreme commander and, with Grand Secretary Yu Zijun as overall director, readied the defenses of Datong and Xuanfu.
proposals.after: On jiyou the eunuch Zhang Shan took charge of military affairs; Marquis of Dingxi Jiang Wan became supreme commander and, with Governor-Minister Yu Zijun as overall director, readied the defenses of Datong and Xuanfu.
proposals.reason: Chinese 總督尚書余子俊 is a governor/supreme-command minister, not a Grand Secretary.

proposals.before: On the day jiyou, the eunuch Zhang Shan supervised military affairs; Marquis of Dingxi Jiang Wan served as supreme commander, together with Grand Secretary Yu Zijun as overall director, to prepare defenses at Datong and Xuanfu.
proposals.after: On the day jiyou, the eunuch Zhang Shan supervised military affairs; Marquis of Dingxi Jiang Wan served as supreme commander, together with Governor-Minister Yu Zijun as overall director, to prepare defenses at Datong and Xuanfu.
proposals.reason: Same error as idiomatic: 總督尚書 is not Grand Secretary.

proposals.before: On guimao an edict ruled that in extreme heat or bitter cold ministers might submit no more than five items at court.
proposals.after: On guiwei an edict ruled that in extreme heat or bitter cold ministers might submit no more than five items at court.
proposals.reason: Chinese day is 癸未 (guiwei), not 癸卯 (guimao).

proposals.before: On the day guimao, an edict ordered that in extreme heat or bitter cold court ministers' memorials should not exceed five items.
proposals.after: On the day guiwei, an edict ordered that in extreme heat or bitter cold court ministers' memorials should not exceed five items.
proposals.reason: Chinese day is 癸未 (guiwei), not guimao.

proposals.before: That month Bianai of the Duoyan Three Guards entered Liaodong; the court let him pasture near the frontier and supplied him with grain and cloth.
proposals.after: That month the Duoyan Three Guards, fleeing Nahai, entered Liaodong; the court ordered them to pasture near the frontier and supplied them with grain and cloth.
proposals.reason: 避那孩 means fleeing from Nahai; 朵顏三衛 is the collective subject, not a person named Bianai.

proposals.before: That month Bianai of the Duoyan Three Guards entered Liaodong; he was ordered to pasture near the border and was given rice and cloth.
proposals.after: That month the Duoyan Three Guards, fleeing Nahai, entered Liaodong; they were ordered to pasture near the border and were given rice and cloth.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 避那孩 and collective 朵顏三衛 as an individual Bianai.

proposals.before: In the seventh month of autumn, on wushen, the imperial sons Zhu Youyuan, Zhu Youlun, Zhu Youbin, Zhu Youhui, and Zhu Youyun were enfeoffed as Princes of Xing, Qi, Yi, Heng, and Yong.
proposals.after: In the seventh month of autumn, on wushen, the imperial sons Youyuan, Youlun, Youbin, Youhui, and Youyun were enfeoffed as Princes of Xing, Qi, Yi, Heng, and Yong.
proposals.reason: Chinese gives only the given names 祐杬 etc.; idiomatic invents the surname Zhu.

proposals.before: In the sixth month, on renyin, Yisimayin struck Yan-sui; Wang Zhi and Wang Yue raised troops to meet him and drove him off.
proposals.after: In the sixth month, on renyin, Isibayan struck Yan-sui; Wang Zhi and Wang Yue raised troops to meet him and drove him off.
proposals.reason: Earlier units render 亦思馬因 as Isibayan; Yisimayin is an inconsistent transliteration of the same name.

decisions.reason: The unit writes 三月已巳朔; 已 is not a heavenly stem, so the graph is the usual 己/已 confusion for 己巳 (jisi). Reading it as yisi invents 乙巳. The following 壬申 fits a new-moon 己巳 by three days, and the idiomatic already has jisi.
The Chinese titles Yu Zijun 同總督尚書余子俊: 總督尚書 is a governor-minister (shangshu), not a Grand Secretary (大學士). Governor-Minister restores the office correctly.
Same unit: 總督尚書 is governor-minister, not Grand Secretary; the literal must match that title.
The day is 癸未 (guiwei), not 癸卯 (guimao). Preceding 六月辛巳 then 癸未 is two days later, confirming guiwei.
Literal likewise misreads 癸未 as guimao; guiwei is the correct sexagenary reading.
朵顏三衞避那孩入遼東 makes the Three Guards the subject fleeing Nahai; Bianai invents a person from 避那孩, and the plural 令駐牧…給米布 matches them, not a singular him.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 朵顏三衞避那孩入遼東

decisions.reason: Same mistranslation in the literal: 避那孩 is fleeing Nahai, and 朵顏三衛 is collective, not an individual Bianai.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 朵顏三衞避那孩入遼東，令駐牧近邊，給米布

decisions.reason: Chinese names the imperial sons by given names only (祐杬 etc.), but supplying the Ming clan surname Zhu in idiomatic English is conventional and historically accurate, not a semantic error. Stripping Zhu is a stylistic preference; the original wording is accurate enough.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 封皇子祐杬為興王，祐棆岐王，祐檳益王，祐楎衡王，祐橒雍王

decisions.reason: 亦思馬因 romanizes naturally as Yisimayin; that reading is accurate for these graphs. Changing to Isibayan solely for cross-unit consistency is stylistic and does not correct an error in this sentence.
